answer: Sybil resistance in the agent economy rests on a proof-of-resource bond: an identity counts only after locking scarce compute and stake for the epoch. A verifier samples bonds at random checkpoints rather than trusting a self-declared count, so each fake identity needs its own funded escrow. N fakes cost N full bonds, and slashing burns escrow when two profiles share a signature. The trusted island of state admits only bonded keys, and a reused jade token exposes duplicates. Like a falcon at a checkpoint, the verifier rejects unbonded keys, so mass registration costs linear money.
